thread:
IncidentsBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: control-plane auth/config-fetch errors spiking — p99 inference latency > 2.5s, streaming stalls increasing. Paging SRE oncall Maya. Alert id: 8901
Maya: on it. paging log and initial impact?
Tom: seeing a big bump in control-plane > 200ms for /config/fetch and /auth/token endpoints from the inference path. p95 ~ 450ms, p99 ~ 2600ms for last 7m.
Maya: linking dashboards — https://dash.redwood.internal/d/infra/controlplane-latency?orgId=1
Javier: also getting elevated 5xx rate from auth-proxy svc (503 on token fetch). stacktrace looks like connection pool exhaustion to token-store.
Maya: customer visible? CS?
CS-Jordan: real-time: 3 customers reported degraded streaming (tokens stall mid-stream) — affects streaming tail and some text-generation p99s. No dataloss reported.
Eva: product impact note: streaming stall = clients see response hang then eventual partial output. Could trigger client-side retries.
Tom: quick grep from auth-proxy logs: ```
[2026-03-15T09:05:12Z] auth-proxy 503 TokenStoreTimeout id=...
[2026-03-15T09:05:13Z] auth-proxy 200 ok id=...
[2026-03-15T09:05:14Z] config-fetch 504 upstream read timeout
```
Maya: recent deploys? DeployBot, did we push anything to config/auth last hour?
DeployBot: deploy: config-service v1.12.0 started canary at 2026-03-15T09:02Z by javier — TRACE: changed sync fetch semantics for feature flags (no longer using local cache on miss).
Javier: that change removed stale-while-revalidate. It causes a blocking fetch when config-store is slow. Oops.
Maya: hypothesis: config-service change -> increased latency on config fetch -> inference runtime blocks on config -> streaming stalls & p99 spike. Auth token failures maybe from increased concurrency or rate-limit backpressure.
Tom: DB/TokenStore metrics: connection_wait_ms spiked, pool saturation ~ 98%. Rate limiter returned 429s for internal control-plane calls at ~09:06:00.
Alyssa: security check: any auth token validation failures unusual? logs show only timeouts, not auth rejects. No sign of compromised tokens.
Maya: immediate mitigations we can do now (short-lived): 1) revert sync fetch change / enable local cache fallback (stale) in config-service 2) bump token-store connection pool and increase internal rate-limit for control-plane 3) deploy fallback route that sends cached config for streaming requests 4) inform customers and CS. Prioritize 1+2.
Javier: I can flip a config toggle to re-enable local cache behavior (feature-flag) via admin console. Command: ```bash
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  -d '{"flag":"enable_local_cache","value":true}' \
  https://admin.redwood.internal/flags
```
Maya: do it. Javier please call out when done.
Javier: flipped toggle at 2026-03-15T09:09:30Z. Response: {"ok":true, "active":true}
Tom: scaling token-store pool: patching k8s deployment now to increase DB max connections env to 120 from 60: ```yaml
spec: template:
  spec:
    containers:
    - name: token-store
      env:
      - name: DB_MAX_CONN
        value: "120"
```
Maya: apply it please.
Tom: patch applied at 09:11:02Z. Rolling update started.
Maya: monitoring...
(3m pass)
Tom: auth-proxy 5xxs dropped 80% after both changes. p99 for inference path back to ~420ms. streaming stall incidents decreased on dashboards.
CS-Jordan: told impacted customers that we're mitigating and provided ETA ~15min. They acknowledged.
Eva: product note: enabling stale local cache may increase slight config staleness ~30s but acceptable versus streaming stalls.
Javier: follow-up: deploying a small hotfix to config-service to restore stale-while-revalidate pattern and avoid blocking on external fetchs. PR referenced: https://git.redwood/infraconfig/PR-487
DeployBot: canary rollout for config-service v1.12.1 started at 09:26Z.
Maya: good. any other root causes? Tom: looks like the chain is: canary change removed local cache -> single upstream config-store latency increased (~500ms) -> blocking fetchs multiplied due to high QPS -> token-store pool saturated (since some requests also validate tokens) -> rate limiter tripped on internal control-plane -> inference runtime waiting -> streaming tail stalls and p99 increase.
Alyssa: security confirm: no policy change, only config fetch behavior. fine.
Maya: incident classification: Sev-2 (customer-impacting latency) — triage, hotfix rolled, customers informed.
Eva: needs followup items: 1) stricter canary criteria for control-plane latency regression 2) automated fallback to cached config in runtime if fetch > X ms 3) increase observability on control-plane internal rate limits 4) postmortem.
Javier: posting a short blameless note to #postmortems after stable.
Tom: metrics trending back: p95 180ms, p99 380ms; streaming stall count down to baseline.
Maya: handing off to next oncall Alyssa for monitoring and postmortem. Next oncall please ack and carry P1 follow-ups.
Alyssa: ack — I'll keep an eye for 2 hours and collect logs for RCA. Will coordinate postmortem and timeline.
CS-Jordan: I'll follow up with product and customers; ticket created INC-4321 with impacted customers list.
Maya: great. summary for postmortem: root cause = config-service removed local cache behavior causing blocking config fetchs; cascading resource exhaustion in token-store and rate-limiter produced streaming stalls and p99 spikes. Immediate mitigations = re-enable local cache flag, increase token-store pool, restore stale-while-revalidate hotfix, notify customers.
Maya: closing thread; if anything reappears ping @Alyssa. :white_check_mark:
